subject: Ownership playbook & hosting governance — follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightcore.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Ownership playbook & hosting governance — follow-up from demo

Hi Elena — great meeting earlier. Quick recap and clear asks so we can keep momentum: 

1) Who is the economic buyer & approver for hosting/SLAs? (You mentioned Carlos — can you confirm contact + preferred cadence)
2) Procurement path: PO vs SOW? Any standard terms we should expect (payment terms, security addenda)?
3) Security/Compliance — BrightCore asked for SOC 2 and data residency constraints. Please confirm whether SOC2 Type 2 + penetration test report will be enough to move to procurement.
4) Decision criteria we heard today (please confirm):
   - Latency: p95 target for typical LLM calls around 200ms for short prompts; tolerates up to 350ms for long-context jobs
   - Deployment preference: Dedicated GPU pool with VPC connectivity (preferred) or Private on-prem if required by legal
   - Cost target: need to be competitive vs current vendor; approximate budget sensitivity noted in call

Next steps we propose: 
- I will share a one-pager mapping hosting options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) + a short SLA summary (attached).
- Please confirm the owner(s) for procurement and security so we can route the SOC2 and SOW.
- If OK, propose a security deep-dive next week to validate artifacts and define the timeline for sign-off.

Attachments: prod_quick_sla_onepager.pdf (one-page summary)

Thanks — happy to sync.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Elena Morales <elena@brightcore.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcore.ai, security@brightcore.ai, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@brightcore.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ownership playbook & hosting governance — follow-up from demo

Thanks Jonas — good summary. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with Eng and Procurement: 

- Economic buyer / approver: Carlos Reyes (VP Eng) is the final approver for platform spend. I am coordinating the requirements but Carlos will sign.
- Procurement: Our standard is PO for platform subscriptions; for multi-year or enterprise deals we ask for a SOW + PO combination. Standard payment terms are Net 60. We will need Redwood's standard MSA + DPA redlines early in the process.
- Security: SOC2 Type II report is required. We also request a recent penetration test summary (can be redacted). Data residency: must be hosted in US (us-east preferred) for this workload.
- Deployment and SLOs: The team is leaning toward Dedicated (VPC peering) but will consider Private on-prem if legal insists. Concrete latency target the Eng team set for the primary use case: p95 < 220ms for 512-token interactions in production. For batch/long-context jobs they accept higher tails.
- Cost sensitivity: Procurement asked that any proposed pricing deliver at least ~25-30% reduction in effective per-API-call cost relative to their current provider; they are flexible on list prices if unit economics meet this.
- Timeline: We are targeting a decision window of 6–8 weeks (end of July). 

I've attached our internal requirements sheet (internal_req_sheet.xlsx) and looped in procurement/security. Let's plan the security deep-dive — availability next Wednesday or Thursday morning (PDT).

—Elena Morales
VP Product, BrightCore AI
elena@brightcore.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@brightcore.ai>, procurement@brightcore.ai, security@brightcore.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Ownership playbook & hosting governance — follow-up from demo

Internal note + proposed owner assignments. Copying Elena so she sees our plan.

Karthik — can you own outreach to Carlos (economic buyer) this week? Goal: confirm sign-off criteria and obtain a rough procurement timeline (PO decision-maker + finance lead).
Marissa — can you own pricing alignment / baseline econ (we should model both Dedicated and Private outcomes against their volume profile). I can share the one-pager + a quick per-1k-token cost delta table.

Immediate deliverables (48–72h):
- Share SOC2 Type II report + redacted pen-test summary (we have these ready; attaching SOC2 stub).
- Draft SOW template and SLR/SLA options (attached redwood_sla_summary.pdf). Recommend we propose: 
   * Canary rollouts: initial dedicated pool (single region us-east) -> 4-week canary -> scale to multi-AZ
   * p95 latency SLOs: baseline (hosted) numbers vs expected Dedicated numbers; call out quantization/ batching options to hit p95 < 220ms
- Security deep-dive: schedule 60-min call next Wed 2026-06-22 09:00 PDT for artifacts + architecture Qs

Marissa — once you have a short econ summary, flag any pricing exceptions we should present to procurement. Karthik — if Carlos needs a one-pager targeted at execs (ROI + reliability), I'll draft and you can send.

Attachments: redwood_sla_summary.pdf

—Jonas
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightcore.ai>, procurement@brightcore.ai, security@brightcore.ai
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ownership playbook & hosting governance — follow-up from demo

Hi Elena / Procurement / Security — thanks for the clarity. Next steps from our side: 

1) SOC2 + pen test: attaching SOC2 summary now and will provide a redacted pen-test summary within 48 hours.
2) Security deep-dive: propose Wed 2026-06-22 09:00 PDT (60m). Please confirm; we will include our Security Engineering lead and infra architect.
3) Tech benchmark: we can run a short lab benchmark (256 / 512 token profiles) and share p95 numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated within 5 business days. That should let Eng validate the latency requirement.
4) Commercial path: attaching SOW template link — please review and flag any must-have contract items. For procurement, our standard enterprise flow is: SOW -> PO -> onboarding. We can support Net 60 if procurement confirms that in writing; Marissa will surface econ tradeoffs at that point.

Links / Attachments: 
- SOC2_report_2024.pdf (attached)
- SOW template: https://drive.google.com/s/0SOW_template_v2
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/BRIGHT-2475

Please confirm attendees for the security call and preferred time if the proposed slot doesn't work. Carlos — if you'd like a 15-min exec summary before the security deep-dive, happy to schedule this week.

—Karthik Iyer
